editor.help.select: Select the gateway, a node or a link to see it and change it. Use + module on a card, + under a board, or Add node to add what hangs from it. Changes are saved at once; Apply changes builds and flashes what they touch.

editor.revoke.question: Take {name} out of this mesh? Its gateway will refuse its handshake and drop its session.
editor.revoke.help: The board keeps its key and its place in the plan; nothing is rebuilt. Use this for a board that was lost, stolen or replaced.
editor.revoke.is_revoked: {name} is revoked: its gateway refuses it.
editor.revoke.restore_help: Admitting it again lets it open a session with the key it already has.
editor.revoke.not_sent: The gateway's host could not be sent the new node list; restart the gateway to apply it.
editor.key.help: Rotating gives the board its next key under its current session, with no flashing; once it confirms, the old key opens nothing. Use this after a board's key may have been copied. Whoever recorded the board's traffic with the old key can still learn the new one, so for a key known to be stolen, reflash the board as well.
editor.key.rotated: The gateway has heard the board confirm this key.
editor.key.waiting: Waiting for the board to confirm its new key; it gets it the next time its gateway hears it.
editor.key.cannot: This board cannot rotate its key: its firmware has no store for one. Reflash it to give it the current key.
editor.key.not_yet: {name} has not confirmed its last key yet; it can be rotated again once it has.
editor.key.done: {name} will be moved to key epoch {epoch} the next time its gateway hears it.
production.title: Production build
production.is_off: Off: this board is built and flashed as a plain image, which can always be replaced.
production.is_on: On: the next build of this board is a production build, and its flash runs the platform's production steps after you type the board's name.
production.warning: A production flash runs steps that cannot be undone: on an ESP32 it burns eFuses for secure boot and flash encryption, on an RP2350 it writes the boot key's hash into OTP. A board flashed this way never goes back to a plain image, and boots only images signed with the same key: keep the key. Every step is shown, irreversible ones marked, before anything runs.
production.no_mode: This board's platform has no production mode, so it is built as a plain image. Turn the setting off.
production.done_off: Production build off for {name}; its next build is a plain image.
production.key_help: The absolute path of the PEM key on the machine running Mesh: RSA-3072 for ESP32, secp256k1 for RP2350. The file must be readable by its owner only (0600). Mesh keeps the path, never the key, and never in the plan.
production.key_ok: The mesh's signing key is in place.
production.key_bad_path: The signing key must be named by an absolute path of letters, digits, dot, dash, underscore and slash.
production.key_unwritten: The signing key path could not be saved.
production.refused_no_mode: {name} has no production mode on its platform; turn its production build off to build it.
production.refused_key_missing: {name} is built for production, which needs this mesh's secure-boot signing key, and none is in place. Name the key file in the board's Access tab.
production.refused_key_relative: {name} is built for production, and this mesh's signing key is not named by an absolute path.
production.refused_key_open: {name} is built for production, and this mesh's signing key file can be read by others. Make it 0600 first.
production.plan_after_build: The steps of the flash are shown here once the build has finished.
production.steps: What the flash will run, in order:
production.type_name: Type the board name ({board}) to run these steps
production.type_help: Only the exact name continues. Anything else runs nothing.
production.name_wrong: That is not the board's name. Type {board} exactly; nothing was run.
production.name_unwritten: The confirmation could not be written; nothing was run.
